raw_response:
I will mostly start from what has worked for me before and only tweak a little. I farm 12.4 mu, so I cannot gamble too much. Wheat and maize are my steady crops, and I have well water, so I will keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard, because if the stand is weak or the ears are small, that loss is bigger than wasting a bit of fertilizer money. With my years in the field, I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen good results from people around me, not chase anything too new. For wheat, I will feed it a bit heavier because it responds well on my land with water. For maize, I will also keep fertilizer solid, especially nitrogen, because if maize lacks strength after wheat stubble, yield drops fast. Cotton I will keep on a smaller area, manage a little more carefully, and spray more times because insects are always a worry. I will use rotary tillage on most land because it saves labor and fits my family situation better than deep ploughing every time. I am looking for a stable harvest first, not the highest possible one.
